text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: service-discovery errors (SRV lookups) observed in us-east-2a starting ~1861234500. Multiple downstream 5xx and elevated latency. Paging SRE oncall.

katya: oncall here, looking now. any quick context on which stack is affected?

liam: seeing CONSUL agent errors: `rpc error: dial tcp 10.2.48.7:8500: connect: connection refused` from sidecars in us-east-2a. SRV lookups for `grpc-backend.service.` timing out -> retries -> 502s on edge.

aj: confirmed from infra metrics: consul raft peers in that AZ show 2/5 reachable per host metrics. consul agent logs have repeated TLS handshake timeouts to other nodes.

nina: I'm going to start a controlled restart of consul agents on the 3 nodes that show heartbeat loss. Doing canary to avoid electing new leader.

liam: +1, also prep to swap CoreDNS upstreams to the regional resolver fallback. If DNS is stuck, the fallback will let SRV lookups use cached IPs.

katya: what's the impact window? any customer facing SLOs breached yet?

support-ops: tickets from a few prod customers (AcmePay, BoxFleet) hitting intermittent auth failures; they're seeing gRPC UNAVAILABLE and increased timeouts. CS notified account teams.

aj: canary restart command I'm running:
```
kubectl -n infra rollout restart daemonset/consul-agent -l az=us-east-2a --grace-period=30
```
Restarting one node now (node-az2a-08).

nina: started. watching raft health: `consul operator raft list-peers` show one node transiently left, leader still stable for now.

liam: I'm going to patch CoreDNS configmap to add a secondary upstream set and reload. Command: 
```
kubectl -n kube-system patch configmap coredns -p '{"data":{"Corefile":". . . forward . /etc/resolv.conf {\n  health\n  reload\n}"}}'
kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart deployment/coredns
```
(This is a temporary fallback so SRV resolutions don't stall on local agent timeouts).

deploy-bot: deploy job `coredns-fallback-186123` started by liam. CI passing.

katya: ping when the first consul canary is back and whether it rejoined raft. Also we should consider routing traffic away from us-east-2a for latency-sensitive routes while we stabilize.

aj: node-08 is back, consul logs show `member joined: node-az2a-08`. Raft peers at 5/5.

nina: rolling canary completed on node-09 and node-10. All three restarted, they rejoined.

liam: CoreDNS fallback applied and rolled. Early signs: SRV lookup timeouts dropped by ~80% in telemetry.

support-ops: CS reports errors down to near normal for affected customers. Still monitoring.

sre-lead: good work. what's root cause hypothesis? network flaps between consul agents or overloaded control-plane?

aj: initial hypothesis: a misbehaving maintenance job in that AZ saturated control-plane NICs -> increased packet drops -> TLS handshake failures between consul agents. Need to correlate to infra jobs we kicked off at ~1861233000.

katya: open a follow-up issue to trace the maintenance job and schedule deeper packet capture inside the AZ for postmortem. Also add evals for SRV lookup telemetry to Redwood Optimize.

liam: for now I've enabled smart-routing policy to steer 20% of traffic off us-east-2a for grpc control-plane routes until we confirm stability. Patch: `routing.policy.grace: 20 -> us-east-2b/us-west-2`

deploy-bot: routing change applied: policy `steer-186123` rolled to 100% of the 20% bucket.

incident-bot: note: severity set to P2 due to partial customer impact and mitigations in flight.

support-ops: still one larger customer (AcmePay) seeing a handful of errors; CS is coordinating a post-fix validation with them.

nina: we've cleared a stuck KV lock I found on the consul leader: `kv:session lost` followed by `released lock` entries. That may have been amplifying retries.

liam: telemetry over the last 12m shows error rate back to baseline and tail latency normalized. I'm going to remove the CoreDNS fallback in 15m unless we see regression.

katya: agree. I'll start the oncall handoff in 30m to liam for follow-up and postmortem. Action items:
- liam: collect pcap and consul TLS traces from us-east-2a
- aj: correlate maintenance jobs and infra autoscale logs at ~1861233000
- nina: include KV lock findings and steps to clear in the postmortem
- support-ops: list impacted customers and timeline for CS outreach

liam: taking handoff. Oncall until 1861270000. I'll own follow-up.

katya: handing off to liam. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: incident status -> mitigated; monitoring. Closed notifications will follow after postmortem scheduled. :eyes:
